questions.q: What is the central risk in treating every setback as a personal problem?
choices: Students might become less willing to read novels.
Teachers may become more generous with grades.
Schools may ignore unequal access to support.
All learners may stop setting ambitious goals.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 1 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: Why does the writer present two students with similar results?
choices: To question advice that ignores unequal circumstances.
To show that both students should change subjects.
To argue that good results depend only on quiet study.
To suggest assessment is never meaningful.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: What can 'try harder' advice fail to provide?
choices: A clear description of the learning task.
More practice with existing resources.
Encouragement to choose challenging work.
The time and space a student actually needs.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: What concern does the writer raise about measuring every activity?
choices: Students may be forced to read books too slowly.
Enjoyment and curiosity may become performance duties.
Teachers will be unable to set any grades.
Informal debate will always produce disagreement.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: Why could praising only the first student be misleading?
choices: It may confuse available resources with character.
It may make the student work fewer hours.
It proves the second student lacks ambition.
It suggests that both students have equal support.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 2 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: Why is a discussion without agreement a useful example?
choices: It demonstrates that disagreement is always desirable.
It shows that marks can measure any conversation.
It illustrates value without an easily counted outcome.
It proves that reading novels is less demanding.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: How are student responsibility and school support related in the conclusion?
choices: Support removes the need for students to decide.
Responsibility matters only when grades are high.
Students should resolve every difficulty independently.
Support makes students' choices more realistic.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: A school notices some pupils cannot work quietly at home. Which action most fits the text?
choices: Tell all pupils to increase their effort.
Offer supervised space for studying.
Reward only those who improve fastest.
Stop giving students feedback.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: A student reads a novel for enjoyment but gains no grade. What would the writer likely say?
choices: The activity can still be valuable.
The student should record each improvement.
The novel has no educational purpose.
Enjoyment matters only during holidays.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 3 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.

questions.q: A teacher gives vague advice to improve. Which change best follows the conclusion?
choices: Ask students to work longer each evening.
Make everyone repeat the same exercise.
Replace all assignments with tests.
Give clearer feedback and chances to revise.
questions.explanation: Paragraph 4 provides the evidence for this interpretation. Review the relevant statement and how the other options conflict with it.
